title: Corporate and Investment Banking Report 2026: A Golden Window for Growth
gist: BCG projects corporate and investment banking revenue pools of ~$1.1T in 2026 (sixth straight record, +7.2%) growing ~5% a year to ~$1.39T by 2030, with growth rotating toward sponsors and hedge funds and AI expected to free up to 40% of CIB FTE capacity.

insights.claim: Corporate and investment banking revenue pools including NBFIs are on track for about $1.1 trillion in 2026, a sixth straight record year, up 7.2% versus 2025 and well ahead of the roughly 5% five-year trend.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Cycle is strong; bank earnings leverage to CIB remains high near-term.

insights.claim: BCG expects the total CIB revenue pool to reach about $1.39 trillion by 2030, growing roughly 5% per year, with share going to banks that make operating-model changes and clear strategic decisions now.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Dispersion among banks, not the pool size, is the key variable.

insights.claim: CIB has accounted for roughly 46% of revenues for the top seven banks since 2020, making it a core engine within banking groups.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Bank group valuations are tightly linked to CIB cycle health.

insights.claim: Growth is rotating away from traditional corporates toward owners of capital: sponsors and hedge funds are expected to grow 37% and more than 40% cumulatively through 2030, far outpacing the traditional corporate wallet.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Prime-brokerage, financing and markets franchises serving funds stand to gain wallet share.

insights.claim: The line between client and competitor is dissolving as NBFIs compete with banks, substitute for them, or become their most important clients, sometimes within the same relationship.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Competitive dynamics between banks and private credit/non-bank lenders are blurring.

insights.claim: Sponsors and hedge funds increasingly buy advisory, financing, markets and treasury together, rewarding banks that connect products and balance sheet around the client rather than defending each mandate separately.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Integrated-coverage banks have an edge with funds.

insights.claim: Banks with AI-led operating models will capture their fair share of the expanding pool while those still piloting individual tools fall behind; AI could free up as much as 40% of CIB FTE capacity by 2030, mostly in repetitive middle- and back-office roles.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Cost-efficiency divergence among banks is likely to widen; BCG frames it as redeployment, not net head-count cuts.

insights.claim: North America holds the largest CIB pool and widens its lead; Asia-Pacific grows fastest via distinct market-level engines; EMEA diverges by country far more than the regional average suggests.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Regional allocation should be country-specific for EMEA and APAC bank exposure.

insights.claim: Banks face four strategic choices (regions, client segments, build-versus-partner products, depth of AI and data redesign), and the current strength is a 'golden window' to lock in talent, platform standards and client relationships that get harder to dislodge each year.
insights.speaker: Christian Schmid
insights.so_what: Banks that act now compound advantage; laggards risk lasting share loss.
